newsitem.title: UK: Gilts applaud BOE moves but profit-takers loom.
newsitem.headline: Gilts applaud BOE moves but profit-takers loom.

text.p: British gilts and short sterling, sharply higher after a major monetary framework reform was coupled with a widely expected interest rate rise on Tuesday, have rosy long-term prospects, analysts said.
But they said in the short term, profit-takers would dominate and the 10-year yield spread against Bunds, just below 150 basis points, was probably close to its near-term lows.
Chancellor Gordon Brown sanctioned a quarter point rise in interest rates to 6.25 percent and announced moves towards independence for the Bank of England.

The market gave a resounding cheer to the moves which came just two working days after the new chancellor took office. Gilts surged over two points and short sterling rose around eight basis points along the strip.
"Markets are looking to push a lot higher," Norman Beauchamp, head of derivatives at Cooperative Bank, told Reuters Financial Television.
Steven Lewis, chief economist at London Bond Broking, said he expected profit takers to step in and shave some of the recent gains in gilts.

"Its' going to be interesting to see how the U.S. trades when it comes in the market but I think this rally will probably blow itself out and for the rest of the week we will see the profit-takers coming in," he said.

He said the 10-year gilt/Bund spread had proably hit its narrowest levels and would widen once industrial production data came out on Wednesday and the April survey from the Confederation of British Industry was released on Thursday.

"When we come to look again at the underlying fundamentals at the UK economy we shall not like what we see and we shall realise the rate rise that has been implemented is a response to a quite serious potential inflation problem," he said.
By 1141 GMT, the spread was at 145 basis points, 28 basis points narrower that the 173 basis point spread before Tuesday's moves were announced.
Societe Generale gitls analyst Tom Rayner said he expected some profit taking near term to take that spread slightly wider again.
"We could see tighter spreads later this year but short term I'd favour some profit taking and a bit of spread widening," he said.

"There must have been pretty large switching from overseas into gilts to bring the spread in so much," Rayner added. "Perceptions Brown will be the pro-Europe chancellor may have helped that -- but I think that's a bit premature."
He said while the reforms were no doubt positive, some investors may be reading too much into them in terms of the new Labour government's stance on Europe.
"It is one step towards full Bank of England independence, which is a necessary requirement for European Economic and Monetary Union, so that could be helping to push that spread in," he said.
"But that's not the key issue because Labour are still committed to a referendum on EMU."

By 1204 GMT, June gilts were up 2-13/32 points on the day at 113-17, off a new contract high of 113-24 set earlier. September short sterling was up 0.05 at 93.18, implying three month money rates of around 6.80 percent by the end of the third quarter.
Analysts said they expected at least one more quarter point interest rate rise in Britain.
"I think we'll see one or two more quarter point moves throughout the year, and possibly some fiscal tightening in the mini budget," said Rayner.
Richard Koss at MFR Inc. NY, expected at least one more rate rise but added the onus was now on the chancellor to produce fiscal reforms to try and take some of wind out of sterling's sails.

The pound surged to its strongest level since August 1992 on the foreign exchange markets after the Chancellor's news. It was quoted at 2.8288/98 against the mark at 1219 GMT, versus 2.8000 before the rate rise and 2.7966/71 straight after it.
"It's going to be paramount to issue a tight budget," he told RFTV. "My suspicion is that considering how fast Mr Brown has moved we will see a very tight budget."
